sites.why: Rule 7: raw requests.post to another LLM vendor (TypeSafe /v1/systemone, native typed contract) whose only model literal jev-1.13.0 is in Router's catalog; key from TYPESAFE_API_KEY env. Treated like another vendor's SDK with a catalog model rather than rule-2 kept, because moving it would not change the model.

Rule 8: ChatAnthropic on default endpoint, operator key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; model chosen at runtime (arg / HEDGE_FUND_LLM_MODEL / DEFAULT_MODEL, also fallback for unlisted ids) and the Anthropic literals claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5-1 are catalog ids.
Rule 8: ChatOpenAI with base_url=os.getenv('OPENAI_API_BASE') (None -> OpenAI default), key OPENAI_API_KEY; runtime model whose OpenAI literals gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-astra are catalog ids.
Rule 2: ChatDeepSeek goes to DeepSeek's endpoint; the repo's only DeepSeek literal 'deepseek-flash' is not a Router catalog id (catalog has deepseek-v4.1-flash), so rule 7 handoff does not apply.
Rule 7: another vendor's SDK (ChatGoogleGenerativeAI, Gemini API) whose model literal gemini-3.8-flash is in Router's catalog.
Rule 7: another vendor's SDK (ChatXAI) whose model literal grok-4.7 is in Router's catalog.

Rule 2: ChatOpenAI with base_url MOONSHOT_BASE_URL or https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 (non-OpenAI host, Kimi). Kept even though kimi-k3 is a catalog id, because rule 2 precedes rule 7 and this is the OpenAI SDK re-pointed, not another vendor's SDK.
